verdict.rationale: Bento's Python SDK attaches `user_id`, `session_id`, and custom `tags` to every span, can tag spans with feature flags or experiment IDs, and reports cost per run out of the box. The evidence never shows cost or usage actually aggregated or broken down by those metadata dimensions, so attribution is implied rather than documented. Missing for 10: documented cost/usage rollups by user, session, or feature tag; token-usage attribution; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can attribute cost and usage to users, sessions, and features via custom metadata

citations.quote: `init()` accepts `user_id`, `session_id`, and `tags` kwargs. Bento invokes them on every span
Tag spans with experiment IDs, feature flags, anything.
you see cost per run, tool failure rates, drift over prompt versions, and regressions across deploys out of the box.
